introduction: On this Second Sunday after Christmas, the Church invites us to go on contemplating the mystery of the Incarnation. Wisdom, in the first reading, makes her dwelling among God's people; in the Gospel, the eternal Word becomes flesh and lives among us. Paul prays that the eyes of our hearts may be enlightened. As we gather, let us ask God to help us understand more deeply the gift of his Son.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: The Word of God has made his home among us. With trust, let us bring our prayers to the Father.
intentions: For the Church: that she may make Christ known as the true light that enlightens everyone. Let us pray to the Lord.
For teachers, theologians and all who study the faith: that they may grow in wisdom and humility. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who live in darkness, whether through sin, ignorance or despair: that the light of Christ may reach them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who start this year without work, shelter or security: that they may find support and hope. Let us pray to the Lord.
For our community: that, having received grace upon grace, we may share our blessings generously. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Father of glory, your Word has come to dwell among us. Enlighten the eyes of our hearts, and grant the prayers we make in his name. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: God pitched his tent among us
reflection.body:
Christmas is too great a mystery to celebrate in a single day, so the Church keeps a whole season. Today's readings step back from the crib and help us reflect on what happened at Bethlehem.

The first reading comes from the book of Sirach. Wisdom speaks in the first person, describing how she came from the mouth of the Most High and looked for a place to rest among the nations. Then God gives her a command: "He who created me made my tent to rest, and said, 'Let your dwelling be in Jacob, and your inheritance in Israel.'" God's wisdom chose to live among one particular people.

John's Gospel takes up that image. "The Word became flesh and lived among us." The Greek word John uses for "lived" means, literally, "pitched his tent." The eternal Word, through whom all things were made, set up his tent among us, the way Wisdom once came to dwell in Israel. God did not remain distant. He came close enough to be seen, touched and heard.

John also says that the world did not recognise him, and that his own did not receive him. But "the true light that enlightens everyone was coming into the world," and to all who received him he gave the power to become children of God.

Paul's prayer in the second reading is a good prayer for this season. He asks that God may give the Ephesians a spirit of wisdom and revelation, "having the eyes of your hearts enlightened, that you may know what is the hope of his calling." Faith is not only knowing facts about God. It is seeing with the heart.

As the holidays end and daily life resumes, the mystery remains. God has pitched his tent among us, and he has not packed it up. He is with us in the Eucharist, in his word, and in one another. Let us ask for enlightened hearts, to see him there.
